problem: Existing person-following robots rely on emitters/wearable devices or on hard-to-distinguish cues (colour, pose, location), lack personalised target identification, and rarely integrate perception with obstacle-avoiding navigation. MOT trackers are either too slow or cannot re-identify a target that leaves and re-enters the view.
motivation: Mobile collaborative robots in houses and industries must follow a specific human in crowded workplaces without being confused by other people or needing teleoperation. Visual Re-ID is non-intrusive and personalised, and the paper integrates it with gestures and navigation into a full system.
key_idea: Combine YOLACT++ person masking, a per-person online-calibrated Re-ID feature-distance test with a threshold, Kalman-filtered 3D localisation, hand-gesture commands and the ROS navigation stack in a state machine to follow one target person.
insight: An online calibration that fits a per-feature mean/std of the target and sets threshold mean+2std deliberately favours false negatives over false positives, and the Kalman filter bridges brief misses; Re-ID results show precision 0.96 > recall 0.91 for the target class, confirming this bias. Background masking gives cleaner features. Failures arise under strong backlight and poor calibration.
method: Detection: pre-trained YOLACT++ (COCO) gives person masks; the image is multiplied by each mask to remove background before Re-ID.
Re-ID: MMT pre-trained IBN-ResNet-50 (MSMT17), 256-d features; calibration collects images of the target at varying distances, split into a calibration set (mean/std of features) and a threshold set.
Identification: weighted feature distance d=sqrt(1/D sum((x-mu)/sigma)^2); the nearest person below threshold lambda=mu_d+2sigma_d is the target, otherwise no target.
Localization: centroid of the target's segmented point cloud from RGB-D, Kalman filter with expiration time t_exp, transformed into the map frame and projected to a 2D goal.
Gesture detection: Mediapipe 21 hand keypoints (63-d) into an RBF one-vs-one SVM for wait/follow/other, requiring 5 consecutive equal outputs.
Navigation and safety: ROS navigation stack with AMCL; other people are treated as obstacles; safety circle d_safe=1.4*v_max*t_exp (1.25 m) stops the robot.
Decision making: state machine with Steady, Follow, Search (rotate toward the last seen position) and Wait states.

setting.backbone: YOLACT++ (pre-trained, frozen) + IBN-ResNet-50 MMT-pre-trained Re-ID + Mediapipe + SVM classifier
setting.training_data: YOLACT++ on COCO; Re-ID network on MSMT17; SVM on 400 self-collected hand-gesture images; per-target online calibration images at test time
setting.observation: RGB-D (Intel RealSense D415) plus laser scan and odometry for localisation
setting.action_space: navigation goals to ROS navigation stack (continuous velocity, max 0.3 m/s); state machine states
setting.privileged: known empty map of the lab (for AMCL); online calibration of the target

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; only classification metrics for hand gestures (accuracy 0.97) and Re-ID (accuracy 0.94) on self-collected data with 8 subjects, and qualitative path results with 10 people.
results: Hand gesture SVM reaches 0.97 accuracy and Re-ID reaches 0.94 accuracy (target precision 0.96, recall 0.91) on self-collected test sets. The full system ran at 7-10 Hz and followed 10 people in a ~100 m² lab with unknown obstacles and distractors. No quantitative comparison with baselines.
limitations: Fails under strong light pointed at the camera and depends on good online calibration; limited to the camera FOV.
Evaluated qualitatively on few subjects in one lab, one run per person, with no baseline comparison.
Speed drops from 10 Hz to 7 Hz as the number of people grows.
